thinking: The detector is effectively running Hough on a dilated binary validity mask (non-NaN=255, NaN=0), not on true edges (no Canny/gradient). That makes Hough heavily depend on how many aligned nonzero pixels exist along a candidate segment. In the sample, the left-hand side is much sparser/more fragmented (fewer nonzero pixels and larger gaps), so with the current settings many true oblique seams fail to accumulate enough votes (hough_threshold_oblique=50) and/or fail the geometric continuity checks (minLineLength_oblique=100 is long for fragmented segments; maxLineGap_oblique=40 may be too small when gaps are larger). The narrow angle windows (6–9 and -9–-6 deg) also reject slightly different tilts that can happen on the left due to perspective/warping, leaving only the strongest right-side segments. To improve left-side recall while limiting right-side false positives, I lowered the oblique Hough threshold and minimum length and increased maxLineGap, so shorter/broken oblique structures can be linked and accepted. I also slightly widened the oblique angle ranges to tolerate local tilt variation without drifting into near-horizontal clutter. Because this increases sensitivity, I modestly strengthened preprocessing (5x5 kernel, 2 dilation iterations) to connect sparse left-side pixels into coherent segments, and I slightly raised horizontal/vertical Hough thresholds to avoid an explosion of spurious axis-aligned detections caused by the stronger dilation.
